introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0540 FOOD AND NUTRITION 1, JUNE 2024, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, duration one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces in the question booklet.

Aucun corrige officiel : les 50 cles sont deduites du programme O Level Food and Nutrition. Aucun calcul numerique dans ce sujet (les valeurs energetiques de la question 21, 37 kJ/g pour un lipide et 17 kJ/g pour un glucide ou une proteine, sont les valeurs classiques du cours).

Le sujet imprime des fautes recopiees telles quelles dans les enonces et options : Fiber, Hor d'ouvre, Savour meal, Based units, Ressin (question 37, probablement Rennin mal ecrit : la cle d reste Rennin), desert (question 42 : dessert), `Vitamin B2` (question 17), "maybe" (question 29). Cles raisonnees mais discutables, a relire par un enseignant de Food and Nutrition : 10 (denatured, sens chimique ; set up et coagulate decrivent le resultat physique), 11 (fibre plutot que vegetable), 16 (poaching, « minimum amount of liquid » ; simmering est voisin), 23 (oxidation, seule option plausible), 29 (telephone pour une fete informelle), 32 (dehydrated foods ; ready to eat foods est voisin), 40 (invalid ; les adolescents ont aussi des besoins particuliers), 41 (steaming plutot que boiling), 43 (snacks plutot que refreshment), 47 (stiff dough plutot que soft), 1 (soya beans, seule proteine vegetale de haute valeur biologique).
Question 49 : la cle d (stomach) suppose que la lettre manquante imprimee devant Stomach est D ; cet ordre est le seul coherent avec les trois autres options (Mouth, Ileum, Duodenum).

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 18, 28, 31, 50. 18 : fats are absorbed in the small intestine through the villi into the lacteals (lymph), four options defendable (cle visee d). 28 : fats give satiety value but protein is also satiating (cle visee a). 31 : la reponse attendue est « fitted units », absente des options ; aucune lettre n'est etablie. 50 : le tissu conjonctif (collagene), lie a l'age de l'animal, est la cause ; tendons, fibres musculaires et age sont tous defendables (cle visee b).
Seconde passe faite : les 4 pages relues en image, enonces et options compares un a un au sujet, chaque question resolue une deuxieme fois sans ecart de cle.

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the foods below is an example of high biological value protein:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Proteins of high biological value contain all the essential amino acids in the right proportions. Most of them come from animal foods (meat, fish, eggs, milk), and soya beans are the one plant food that also gives a complete protein. Legumes and pulses are good sources of protein but are low in one or more essential amino acids, and gelatine lacks tryptophan, so these three are proteins of low biological value.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of a diet is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A diet is a particular way of eating, planned for a purpose or a health need. A low-fat diet is a true diet (it is followed to control weight or blood cholesterol). Fast foods and convenience foods are types of food, and reheated diet is not a recognised diet.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is solid at room temperature?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Lipids are the whole group of fats and oils. A lipid that is solid at room temperature is called a fat (for example butter or lard), while a lipid that is liquid at room temperature is called an oil. "Lipid" is the general term and a fatty acid is a building block of a fat, so neither names the solid form.

**Answer: B.**
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Pellagra is generally common in a ______ eating population.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Pellagra is caused by a lack of niacin (vitamin B3). In maize the niacin is bound and cannot be absorbed, and maize is also poor in tryptophan (the amino acid the body can change into niacin). Populations that live mainly on maize, with little meat, milk or eggs, are therefore the ones in which pellagra is common.

**Answer: D.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Cereals are ______ of cultivated grasses.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cereals (rice, maize, wheat, millet, sorghum, oats) are the edible seeds or grains of cultivated grasses. Wheat is only one example of a cereal, and pulses are the seeds of leguminous plants, not of grasses.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the parts of a pressure cooker is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A pressure cooker is made of a pan with a tightly fitting lid, a rubber sealing ring (gasket), a control valve (weight), a safety valve and a trivet, the perforated stand that keeps the food out of the water at the bottom. A vacuum seal and a cork are not parts of a pressure cooker.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cooking method that combines roasting and stewing is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In braising the meat is first browned in a little hot fat (as in roasting) and is then cooked slowly in a small amount of liquid in a covered pan (as in stewing). Simmering is gentle boiling, basting is spooning hot fat over food while it roasts, and frying is cooking in hot fat.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An additive that stops rancidity is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rancidity is the unpleasant smell and taste of fats and oils that have combined with oxygen. Antioxidants (for example vitamin C and vitamin E) slow down this oxidation, so they keep fats from going rancid. Stabilizers and emulsifiers keep mixtures smooth and prevent separation, and gelatine is a setting agent.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Vitamin C aids in the absorption of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) helps the body to absorb iron from plant foods, which is why a source of vitamin C (an orange or a tomato) is eaten with a meal of beans or green vegetables. It plays no such role for phosphorus, iodine or fluorine.

**Answer: D.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: When proteins are heated, their chemical structure is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Heat breaks the bonds that hold the folded protein molecule in shape, so its chemical structure is denatured (unfolded). The visible result of denaturation is coagulation: the protein sets and becomes firm and opaque, as when an egg white is boiled. The question asks about the chemical structure, so the answer is denatured. Gelatinisation is what happens to starch when it is heated in water.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Dietary guidelines show that ______ should be taken to prevent intestinal disorders.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fibre (roughage) is not digested, but it adds bulk to the food residues and helps them move through the intestine. A diet rich in fibre prevents constipation and other intestinal disorders. Water and vegetables help, but fibre is the nutrient named by the dietary guidelines for this purpose.

**Answer: A.**
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown: The adult bone malformation is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Osteomalacia is the softening and bending of the bones of adults, caused by a lack of vitamin D (and calcium). Rickets is the same type of deficiency but in growing children, scurvy is a lack of vitamin C, and dementia is a brain disorder, not a bone disease.

**Answer: A.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: The most commonly used form of sugar in cooking is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sucrose (table sugar, obtained from sugar cane or sugar beet) is the sugar used to sweeten drinks and to make cakes, jams and puddings. Fructose is fruit sugar, glucose is the sugar in the blood and lactose is milk sugar.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A deficiency of retinol in the body can cause:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Retinol is vitamin A. A lack of it causes night blindness and, if it continues, permanent blindness (xerophthalmia). Anaemia is caused by a lack of iron, scurvy by a lack of vitamin C and pellagra by a lack of niacin.

**Answer: C.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: This provides essential nutrients and immunity to new born babies.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Colostrum is the thick yellowish first milk that the mother produces in the first days after birth. It is rich in protein and contains antibodies that protect the baby against infections (immunity). Ordinary milk comes later, and water and cereal give no immunity.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cooking in minimum amount of liquid at a temperature below boiling point is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Poaching means cooking food gently in the minimum amount of liquid, kept just below boiling point (the liquid hardly moves). It is used for eggs, fish and fruit. Simmering uses plenty of liquid kept at about boiling point with small bubbles, steaming cooks in the steam above the water, and braising cooks browned food slowly in a covered pan.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Scurvy is the deficiency of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Scurvy (bleeding gums, slow healing of wounds, tiredness) is caused by a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid), found in citrus fruits, guava, tomatoes and fresh vegetables.

**Answer: B.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown:
The absorption of fats in digestion takes place in the:

*Options as printed:* A) Ileum   B) Lymph   C) Villi   D) Small intestines
questions.corrige_markdown:
After fats have been digested to fatty acids and glycerol, they are absorbed in the small intestine, through the villi (the finger-like projections of its wall), into the lacteals, which are lymph vessels. Four of the printed options can be defended (the ileum is a part of the small intestine, the villi absorb, and the lymph carries the fats away), so no single letter is established.

**Intended answer: D (Small intestines).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown: To ease work in the kitchen, it must be well:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A kitchen that is well planned has the sink, cooker and refrigerator close together and the work surfaces in a logical order (the work triangle), so that less time and energy are used and the work is easier.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An elastic stretch protein found in wheat is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Gluten is the protein of wheat flour. When flour is mixed with water it becomes elastic and stretchy and traps gas, which is why bread dough rises. Casein is the protein of milk and albumin is the protein of egg white.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following classes of food has a higher calorific value?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Per gram, fat gives about 37 kJ (9 kcal), whereas protein and carbohydrate (starch) give only about 17 kJ (4 kcal) each. Vitamins give no energy. Fats therefore have the higher calorific value.

**Answer: B.**
themes: energy value of food and energy needs

questions.enonce_markdown: The nutrient necessary for growth and repairs of worn out tissues is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Proteins are the body-building nutrients: they supply the amino acids needed to make new cells for growth and to repair worn out or damaged tissues.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Enzymes speed up food decay through:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The enzymes that are naturally present in foods bring about chemical changes such as oxidation (for example the browning of a cut apple or banana, and the ripening and softening of fruits), which makes the food decay. Evaporation and transpiration are loss of water and neutralization is the reaction of an acid with a base, so none of these is how enzymes cause decay.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of a labour saving device is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A labour saving device is an electrical appliance that does a job quickly and saves the effort of doing it by hand. A blender does the work of pounding, mashing and mixing, so it is the labour saving device. A knife is a hand tool, and a boiler and a kettle only heat water.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Three gases used in raising mixtures are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Mixtures such as cakes, bread and pastry rise because a gas expands inside them: air (beaten or folded in), carbon dioxide (from yeast or baking powder) and steam (formed from the water in the mixture when it is heated). "Gas" and "oxygen" are not the raising agents used, and powder is not a gas.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Heat can be transferred rapidly in liquids and gases through:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In liquids and gases the heated part becomes lighter and rises while the cooler part sinks, which sets up currents that carry heat quickly through the whole of the liquid or gas. This transfer is convection (as in a pan of boiling water or an oven). Conduction occurs mainly in solids, and radiation travels as waves.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The transformation of food by a series of activities is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Food processing is the series of activities (cleaning, cutting, cooking, drying, canning, packing...) by which raw foods are changed into food products. Food production is the growing or rearing of the raw foods.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which nutrient provides a feeling of fullness?

*Options as printed:* A) Fats   B) Carbohydrates   C) Water   D) Protein
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fats stay in the stomach longer than other nutrients because they are digested slowly, so a meal that contains fat gives a feeling of fullness (satiety value) and delays hunger. Protein is also satisfying, so the printed question does not make one single option certain.

**Intended answer: A (Fats).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Invitations for informal parties may be given through:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An informal party (a family or friends gathering) does not need a formal invitation: a telephone call or a spoken invitation is enough. Written, printed and invitation cards are used for formal occasions such as weddings and official dinners.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A man who serves customers at the table in a restaurant is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A waiter takes orders and serves food to customers at the table in a restaurant. A caterer supplies food for functions, a receptionist welcomes guests at a desk and a steward looks after passengers or serves on ships and aircraft.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Kitchen units that are fixed to the walls and floors are:

*Options as printed:* A) Tall units   B) Peninsular units   C) Island units   D) Based units
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks for fitted (built-in) units, which are fixed to the walls and floor, as opposed to free-standing units that can be moved. That word is not among the printed options, and the options name positions of units (tall, peninsular, island, base), so no single letter is established.

**Intended answer: fitted (built-in) units, which is not one of the printed options.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Instant foods are examples of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Instant foods (instant coffee, instant noodles, instant mashed potato, soup powders) have had their water removed, so they are dehydrated foods that are made ready in a moment by adding hot water. Canned and frozen foods are preserved by other methods and still contain water.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Poor teeth formation can be prevented by eating foods rich in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Calcium (with phosphorus and vitamin D) is the mineral that builds hard, strong teeth and bones, so foods rich in calcium such as milk, small fish eaten whole and green vegetables prevent poor formation of the teeth. Iodine prevents goitre and iron prevents anaemia.

**Answer: C.**
themes: dental health and diet in nutrition

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following vitamins is readily destroyed by heat?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vitamin C is water-soluble and is easily destroyed by heat, by air and by long cooking. For this reason vegetables and fruits should be cooked for a short time, in a little water, or eaten raw. Vitamins D, E and K are fat-soluble and are much more stable.

**Answer: D.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following helps in jam setting?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A jam sets when sugar, pectin and acid are present in the right amounts. Lemon juice is rich in acid and in pectin, so it is added to fruits that are low in them. The other juices do not give enough acid and pectin to help the setting.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The meat from bush animals is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Meat from wild (bush) animals and birds is called game. Pork is the meat of the pig, mutton the meat of a sheep and veal the meat of a young calf.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which enzyme is responsible for milk coagulation?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rennin is the enzyme (found in the stomach of calves) that curdles milk by coagulating the casein, and it is used in cheese making. Lipase digests fats and pepsin digests proteins in the stomach. "Ressin" is not an enzyme (it is a misprint of resin or rennin).

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A substance deliberately added to food to improve the quality is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A food additive is any substance deliberately added to food to improve its quality: its flavour, colour, sweetness, texture or keeping quality. Flavours, colours and sweeteners are only particular kinds of additives, so the general answer is food additives.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these vitamins controls haemorrhage?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vitamin K is needed for the clotting of blood, so it stops bleeding (haemorrhage). A lack of it makes a wound go on bleeding.

**Answer: B.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of them require special dietary needs?
questions.corrige_markdown:
An invalid (a sick person) needs a special diet that is light, easy to digest and suited to the illness. The others are healthy people who eat the normal family diet, although adolescents need larger quantities of some nutrients.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The best method of cooking food for an invalid is by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Steaming makes food soft and easy to digest, needs no fat and keeps the flavour and most of the nutrients, which is what a sick person needs. Frying makes food rich and hard to digest, and boiling and stewing lose more nutrients in the water.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A meal that starts with a main dish and ends with a dessert is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A meal with a main dish followed by a dessert has two courses, so it is a two course meal. A three course meal has a starter as well, and an hors d'oeuvre is a starter.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ______ refers to food served between meals.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Snacks are small amounts of food eaten between the main meals (breakfast, lunch and dinner). Lunch is a main meal, and cakes and pastries are only examples of snack foods. Refreshment is a looser word for light food and drinks served on any occasion.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An organism responsible for infecting canned food is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Clostridium (Clostridium botulinum) forms spores that survive in badly processed canned food, because there is no air in the can. It grows there and produces a dangerous poison (botulism). Staphylococcus, E. coli and Salmonella are the usual causes of food poisoning in meat, milk, eggs and handled foods.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The term "kitchen" management means:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Kitchen management covers the whole work of the kitchen: the wise purchase of the food and equipment, the organisation of the work, the cooking and the serving of the food. Options A, B and C each name only one part of this work.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Proper planning and maintenance of kitchen equipment
Wise purchase of kitchen equipment and serving of food
Organisation and purchasing of cooking ingredients
Wise purchase, organisation, cooking and serving of food

questions.enonce_markdown: The function of the control valve of a pressure cooker is ______.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The control valve (the weight on the lid) lets a small amount of steam escape, which keeps the pressure inside the pan constant at the level wanted. The sealing ring stops steam from escaping at the rim, and the trivet keeps the food out of the water.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Allows a small amount of steam to escape from pan
Ensures that no steam escapes from the rim of pan
Ensures that different kinds of food are cooked at a time
Allows food to stand in steam without touching the base of pan

questions.enonce_markdown: The normal dough consistency for a short crust pastry is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Short crust pastry is made by rubbing fat into flour and adding just enough cold water to make a stiff (firm) dough. A soft dough is sticky and makes tough, shrunk pastry, a hard dough is too dry to roll, and an elastic dough (from too much water and handling) makes the pastry tough.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following food service is best for wedding ceremonies?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In buffet service the food is laid out on tables and guests help themselves. It is the best way to feed the large number of guests at a wedding quickly and with few servers. Informal service is for the family at home, and English service (the host serves the guests at the table) suits a small dinner.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Chemical digestion of protein begins in the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Protein digestion begins in the stomach, where pepsin, working with hydrochloric acid, breaks proteins into smaller peptides. There is no protein-digesting enzyme in the mouth, and trypsin acts later in the duodenum. (On the printed paper the letter D is missing in front of Stomach, which is the fourth option.)

**Answer: D.**
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown:
______ is responsible for toughness in meat.

*Options as printed:* A) The size of the cuts   B) The age of the animal   C) Tendons   D) Muscle fibres
questions.corrige_markdown:
The toughness of meat comes mainly from connective tissue (collagen), which increases as the animal gets older and works its muscles more. Cooking by moist heat (stewing, braising) softens it. Because tendons, muscle fibres and the age of the animal are all connected with toughness, the printed options do not give one certain answer.

**Intended answer: B (The age of the animal).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
